media: Below are screenshots from the game, in order: title.jpg, herding-early.jpg, wolf-near.jpg, sunset.jpg, snatch.jpg, end-card.jpg.
first_impression: Looks like an endearing low-poly game jam project about being a good dog, nailing the cozy dusk aesthetic right off the bat. However, it also looks like a 10-minute micro-game on a single static map rather than a fleshed-out commercial game. If you're charging $10, there needs to be a lot more game here than just shooing cubes into a pen three times.
best_things: The picture-in-picture 'Snatch!' alert camera in snatch.jpg is brilliant UI design for showing urgent off-screen peril without feeling disorienting.
The warm golden-hour lighting progression across sunset.jpg and end-card.jpg creates a wonderfully cozy, authentic countryside mood.
Objective tracking and timer pacing in the HUD are clean, instantly readable, and clearly communicate high stakes.

worst_problems.problem: Zero content depth or meta-progression beyond replaying the same single pasture on three difficulty presets.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add a multi-day campaign with changing seasons, different farm layouts, weather events, or cosmetic unlocks for Pip to justify a full purchase.

worst_problems.problem: Intrusive red tutorial banner over-explains the emergency with clunky button reminders that break the pastoral immersion.
worst_problems.suggestion: Rely on the PIP camera and urgent barking/whistle audio cues instead of slapping a massive red text box explaining basic controls mid-run.

worst_problems.problem: The environment feels sterile and barren, relying on repetitive cookie-cutter tree cones and purple bush clusters.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add organic terrain variety like elevation cliffs, tall grass patches to stalk through, and natural obstacles that sheep refuse to cross.

worst_problems.problem: Animals appear stiff and toy-like, with blocky polygonal sheep clumping unnaturally like sliding geometric props.
worst_problems.suggestion: Rework flocking physics to feel like fluid herd behavior and give Pip and the wolves snappier, more expressive run-and-turn animations.

worst_problems.problem: Harsh, jagged twilight shadow cutoff splits the ground awkwardly down the middle instead of casting a soft sunset gradient.
worst_problems.suggestion: Soft-filter directional terrain shadows and blend ambient nightfall lighting so dusk settles organically instead of creating a sharp visual divide.

boredom_points: Patrolling the exact same stone wall border every round once you memorize wolf spawn timings.
Waiting on slow straggler sheep when you already have enough home to clear the tier.
confusions: The dotted red laser line from the wolf in wolf-near.jpg looks like an RTS targeting reticle rather than natural predatory AI.
Unclear whether Pip can actually take damage or get knocked down by wolves, or if the dog is completely invincible.
wish_list: Multiple maps featuring rougher terrain like Scottish moors, rocky cliffs, and river crossings.
Different herding dog breeds with distinct handling attributes like speed, bark radius, or stamina.
Dynamic weather system introducing thick fog, heavy rain, or howling winds that disrupt sheep hearing.
one_line_review: A gorgeous, cozy 15-minute prototype with great dusk vibes, but desperately needs a campaign and multiple maps before asking for ten bucks.
